newsitem.title: INDONESIA: East Timor separatists kill 17 troops in ambush.
newsitem.headline: East Timor separatists kill 17 troops in ambush.

text.p: Rebels opposing Indonesia's rule in the former Portuguese colony of East Timor killed 16 police and a soldier in an ambush on Saturday, police said.
The ambush followed an upsurge of violence in which 17 people died on Wednesday and Thursday as a result of separatist attacks aimed at disrupting Indonesia's general elections in the territory.

East Timor deputy police chief Colonel Atok Rismanto said by telephone from the provincial capital Dili that 16 police and one soldier were killed when a grenade was thrown into a truck travelling in the hills outside the second city of Baucau.
He said another six policemen and one soldier were seriously injured, three policemen slightly injured and only one policeman escaped unharmed in the attack at about 9.45 a.m. (0130 GMT).

"There were 16 policeman killed and one soldier killed. It was a grenade attack with weapons," Rismanto said. "A search operation is already being done by the army but it has not yielded any results."

East Timor police chief Colonel Yusuf Muharam said police had detained 22 suspects -- including 13 "rebels" and nine supporters -- in connection with election-eve violence on Wednesday, the official Antara news agency reported.
"The rebel members who have been detained are those who made the disturbance on the night before the election," Muharam said.
Indonesia occupied East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
Diplomats said separatists had wanted to demonstrate their strength in East Timor, with a population of 850,000, and the result was the worst violence in the territory in years.
One diplomatic source said it was unclear whether the latest ambush signalled a longer-term escalation of violence.
Antara also reported that Indonesia replaced its army commander in East Timor on Saturday.
Diplomatic analysts said it appeared to be a routine change of command unconnected to the violence.
Antara said Colonel Mahidin Simbolon surrendered his command of the Wira Dharma military district in a ceremony in Dili after a two-year tour of duty.

Simbolon, a special forces officer appointed to the position in May 1995, came to prominence in 1992 for his key role in the capture of East Timorese rebel leader Xanana Gusmao, now serving a 20-year prison term in Jakarta.
Antara said he would be replaced soon by infantry Colonel Slamat Sidabutur, currently on a training course.

The Indonesian military, which maintains a strong presence in East Timor, says about 80 poorly armed guerrillas remain in the rugged hills in the territory. Other sources suggest there are around 200.
Jakarta officially has five full battalions of troops as well as other units in East Timor numbering around 5,000 men, far more than in neighbouring provinces with much larger populations.
